transcript.content: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. What brings you in to see me today?

Well, I called the Employee Assistance Program because I've been having this issue at work. I'm a supervisor, so I'm in the office a lot, and lately, every little bang or noise just... it really gets to me. Like, if someone slams a file drawer shut or drops a coffee mug, I jump hard. And then my heart just keeps racing in my chest for way longer than it normally should after something like that. It's just been really throwing me off.
Did these startle reactions and racing heart start after something stressful or traumatic happened to you, or have they been building up gradually over time?

It didn't really build up, no. It definitely started after something specific happened. This has been going on for about two weeks now, ever since... well, I had a late-night confrontation with my regional boss. That's exactly when all this started.
Since that confrontation with your boss two weeks ago, have you been having unwanted memories or flashbacks of that event that pop into your mind, even when you don't want them to?

No, I haven't noticed anything like that. I mean, I remember the argument, obviously, but I'm not getting flashbacks or having memories of it just force their way into my head out of nowhere. My mind isn't really getting stuck on the event itself, it's just... mostly that physical jumpiness I mentioned.
On days when nothing particular happens at work, do you notice that you're feeling anxious or on edge throughout the day, or does the anxiety mainly happen when you hear a sudden noise?

It's definitely more than just the noises. I feel pretty on edge throughout the whole day. Like, when I'm in the office now, I just... I keep checking where my boss is. I catch myself looking at where the exits are, or turning to see whether anyone is coming up behind me. I'm doing this even when I'm at my desk and supposed to be focused on my team. So yeah, I'm definitely tense even when it's completely quiet.
When you're away from work—at home, running errands, or on the weekend—do you still feel that same sense of being on edge and tense, or does it mainly happen when you're at the office?

No, not really. It's... it's pretty much just at the office. When I'm at home or, you know, out doing things on the weekend, I don't really feel that same tension. I guess once I'm away from work and know I won't run into him, I can actually relax a bit. So yeah, it's mainly just when I'm in the building.
Have you thought about calling in sick to work, or have you actually missed any days at the office since this started two weeks ago?

No, I haven't called in sick or missed any days. I'm still making it in every day. But... I'm definitely struggling once I'm there. I'm just a lot slower with my accounts and making staffing decisions. I've actually had to ask my team to double-check things that I would normally just handle on my own. It's frustrating, and honestly, with performance reviews coming up soon, I'm pretty worried that these mistakes are going to end up affecting my job.
Have you thought about changing your schedule, working from home, or asking to be reassigned away from your boss—and if so, have you actually made any of those requests?

No, I haven't really... I haven't made any requests like that. I guess I haven't thought about asking to work from home or trying to change my schedule around. And I definitely haven't asked HR or anyone to be reassigned. I've just been trying to push through it and keep showing up to my normal shifts, even though it's been tough.
Even though you haven't missed days or requested reassignment, have you found yourself avoiding certain areas of the office, certain times of day, or situations where you might encounter your boss?

No, not really. I mean, I guess I haven't been going out of my way to avoid him or certain parts of the building. I just go where I need to go to get my work done. If I see him, I see him. I haven't been hiding in the breakroom or taking different hallways or anything like that.
Have you noticed any changes in your sleep since this started two weeks ago—such as trouble falling asleep, waking up during the night, or waking up earlier than usual?

No, my sleep has been pretty normal, actually. I haven't had any trouble falling asleep, and I usually sleep straight through the night like I always do. I haven't been waking up early either. So, no real changes there.
Even when you're at home or away from work, do you find yourself thinking about the confrontation with your boss, or worrying about what might happen when you go back to the office?

No, not really. I mean, when I'm home, I just kind of leave work at work. I watch TV, hang out, do my normal stuff. I'm not sitting around replaying what happened or stressing about going in the next day. It's just... I just don't really think about it much when I'm not there.

You mentioned that your work performance has slowed down and you've had to ask your team to double-check things. On a scale of 1 to 10, how much would you say this situation is interfering with your ability to do your job as a supervisor compared to how you normally function?

I'd say maybe a 4 or a 5 out of 10. Like I said, I'm still making it to work and getting through the day, but I'm definitely slower with the accounts and making staffing decisions. I just second-guess myself a lot right now. That's why I've had to ask my team to double-check things that I'd normally just handle on my own without a second thought. And, honestly, with performance reviews coming up soon, I'm pretty worried that these little mistakes or delays are going to end up affecting my job.

When you're at work and feeling that tension and jumpiness, do you feel like your reactions are making sense given what happened with your boss, or do you feel like you're overreacting to things that shouldn't really bother you this much?

I'm not really sure, to be honest. I guess I haven't really thought about it like that. It's just... it just happens. I don't know if it makes sense or if I'm overreacting to things. I just know that's how I've been feeling when I'm in the office right now.
